Subject: RE: Initial DR & SLA questions for NovaRetail deployment

Emma / Paul —

Thanks for the helpful kickoff earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the ask in writing so we can align across product, SRE, and procurement: NovaRetail is requesting a contract-level commitment for cross-region failover that guarantees both high availability and defined RTO/RPO for your primary US region. Specifically you asked about: 1) an RTO target of 10–15 minutes for automated cross-region failover and 2) an RPO of near-zero for session state/critical KV.

Two quick notes so expectations stay aligned:
- Our hosted default SLA covers single-region uptime and regional failover behavior (automatic routing to alternative capacity) but it does not include a guaranteed 10–15 minute end-to-end RTO for region-to-region failover without a dedicated configuration.
- Providing a firm 10-minute RTO with near-zero RPO requires either hot-standby multi-region deployment or an agreed warm-standby with synchronous replication for critical state. Both options affect cost and reserved capacity commitments.

Can you confirm which of the following you prefer so we can model costs and a formal exception path?
1) Prioritized multi-region (hot) with reserved capacity in 2 regions — SLA: 99.99% cross-region availability, RTO <= 10 min, RPO <= 1s for KV (billing uplift).
2) Warm-standby (near-warm) with active-passive replication — SLA: 99.95% with targeted RTO <= 30 min, RPO <= 5 min for critical artifacts.
3) Keep hosted on standard configuration and accept application-level retry/resilience with best-effort failover (no contractual RTO/RPO).

If you confirm option 1 or 2 we'll put the details into a mutual action plan and kick off a small technical PoC to validate failover timing.

Thanks — will loop Neha on the commercial side after your selection.

Regards,

Priyom —

Thanks, this was very clear. Our preference is option 1 (hot multi-region) for the following reasons:
- Our checkout and inventory lookups are latency-sensitive and cannot tolerate tail risk during failover.
- We have compliance requirements for order auditability; losing even a few minutes of event capture will break downstream reconciliation.

That said, we understand the cost implications. Two asks before we commit:
1) A detailed target cost delta (monthly) for hot hot-east/ hot-west dual-region versus warm-standby.
2) A proposed runbook excerpt that shows the automated failover steps and a sample RTO measurement from a previous customer (anonymized).

We'll share our compliance team's specific RPO constraints separately, but assume they will push for RPO <= 1s for critical tables.

Best,

Hi all —

Technical summary from SRE/Infra perspective:
- Hot multi-region with synchronous replication for everything (RPO <=1s) is only feasible if NovaRetail agrees to dedicated reserved pools in both regions and accepts the cost uplift. Synchronous cross-AZ or cross-region replication at the token/embedding layer is very expensive and increases write latency unless we adopt an eventual-consistency pattern for non-critical state.
- Practical hybrid approach: keep read-heavy caches replicated asynchronously (near-zero perceived RPO) and synchronous replicate a small set of critical objects (cart session, order ledger pointer) — that keeps RTO in the 10–15 min range for full failover while bounding cost.
- RTO drivers: DNS propagation, routing weight transfer, KV cold-warm cache warming, and model cold-starts on spare GPUs. We typically see ~8–12 minutes for automated routing + cache/Warmed-model provisioning in our prior tests with warm standby images ready. Achieving <5 minutes end-to-end requires fully warmed hot instances and pre-allocated GPU pools (hot hot).

Action items for NovaRetail PoC:
1) Identify the exact critical keys (table/list) that need synchronous replication.
2) Validate traffic shaping to accept slightly higher write latency (if needed) in exchange for synchronous replication.
3) Confirm capacity reservation window (hours/day) for smoke-failover tests.

I'll attach a short excerpt from our runbook and a sample failover timeline.

—Aditya

We reviewed the technical approach and commercial implications, and Redwood can offer a contract amendment that includes a cross-region resilience SLO under the following conditions:

1) Deployment: Hot multi-region (active-active) with reserved GPU capacity in us-east-1 and us-west-2 scoped to NovaRetail.
2) SLO: Cross-region availability target of 99.99% for API endpoints, with an RTO guaranteed <= 15 minutes for automated failovers when smoke tests are passed. RPO will be contractual for a defined critical set: <= 1s for identified keys (to be captured in an appendix).
3) Operational requirements: Quarterly failover drills (>=2/year) with signed runbook and timestamped RTO/RPO reports; Redwood will provide the drill report artifacts.
4) Commercial: A reserved capacity uplift and a 12-month committed term for the reserved pools; we will share a detailed cost delta in the commercial appendix and include a 60-day notice clause for capacity scaling.

Next steps — Priyom will send an updated MSA amendment and a mutual action plan that includes the appendix for the critical keys and the runbook excerpt. We will also provide a sample drill report from a prior customer (redacted).

If this aligns, please confirm and we will aim to have the amendment in the signature queue within two weeks.
